title: Technology & SaaS
meta_description: Dataq Software programs for Technology & SaaS: priority use cases, regulatory posture and delivery model.

blocks.x: Release velocity and unit economics decide survival — we build the data, AI and platform engineering that scales with your product, not against it.
Where the industry stands

Software companies eat their own cooking or get eaten: platform engineering, SRE discipline and FinOps are not nice-to-haves but the operating system of companies whose product is infrastructure. The AI era adds a new economics layer — inference cost per customer, model quality per feature, data moats per vertical — that decides which SaaS companies compound margin and which dilute it.
The pressure is structural

The competitive math is unforgiving: NRR (net revenue retention) is decided by product velocity and reliability; enterprise procurement gates on SOC 2/ISO 27001 evidence; AI features must launch in weeks against well-funded rivals while keeping unit economics sane. Meanwhile data products — benchmarks, telemetry insights, vertical datasets — have become a second revenue line for companies that can build the privacy and entitlement plumbing.
How Dataq Software responds

Dataq Software works with SaaS and platform companies, fintech-adjacent teams, semiconductor and hardware firms, and gaming studios: platform engineering and DevEx programs, AI feature factories with evaluation puts to work, data monetization stacks, security and compliance automation, and scaling engineering for the moments when growth tests architecture.
Pressure points we hear most

items: Velocity vs. reliability tension
Deploy frequency rises while incident load eats roadmap; error budgets exist in slide decks, not in release policy.
AI features ship without economics
Teams bolt on LLM features with no cost telemetry, no eval put to work and no guardrails; margins erode silently per customer.
Data moat unrealized
Usage telemetry accumulates but never becomes product; data products stall on privacy questions and entitlement plumbing.
Compliance gates enterprise deals
SOC 2/ISO 27001 evidence assembled manually per audit; security questionnaires consume engineering weeks per quarter.
Cloud unit economics opaque
Cost per customer, per tenant, per feature unknown; gross margin surprises surface in board decks.
Support and success scale linearly
Customer support and CS operations grow headcount with ARR; ticket deflection without resolution raises churn risk.

blocks.x: How a delivery runs

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
